review_notes: I read the whole file (lines 1–86). It has two declarations: the private helper `bu_spatialPartial_add` and the theorem `bu_spatialSecondPartial_mul_full`. Neither has a `@[simp]` attribute, and the file defines no simp set. I also looked at the related lemmas `CKN.Core.Step3.spatialPartial_mul_full` and `spatialPartial_add_at`, which have no simp attributes either. Each of the two declarations needs smoothness hypotheses (`ContDiff ℝ ⊤`) on the functions involved. A bare simp lemma would have to discharge those side conditions, and the functions are arbitrary. Adding `@[simp]` would be speculative, so I did not recommend it. No rewrite direction is wrong, no pair of rules competes, and there is no cycle or unwanted expansion. The private helper `bu_spatialPartial_add` looks redundant with `spatialPartial_add_at` in `CarlemanCoreMixed.lean`, which takes weaker `DifferentiableAt` hypotheses. That is a duplication or reuse issue, outside this rubric, so I did not report it. I did not check whether the repo's simp set is used elsewhere to normalize `spatialSecondPartial` of a product, so I can't rule out a simp-interface concern there.
